cases.description: Only required fields. Steps with no end wait for the athlete.
1 min work, 30 s rest, x5 with no final rest: once as a block loop, once as sets. 420 s each.
Defaults, a get-ready rest, rest between rounds replacing the round's last rest, and skipLastRest. 10 + 280 + 280 + 220.
Rep-based sets with per-set targets, rest after every set, a superset with one side at a time, and a rest between rounds appended when no rest ends the round.
Per-set end and rest, with the final rest skipped. 40 + 20 + 30 + 15 + 20.
Two Tabatas. The outer loop's rest and skip act on the inner loop's last rest. 240 - 10 + 60 + 240 - 10.
restBetweenRounds as a list of two, repeating: 60, 90, 60. 4 x 30 + 60 + 90 + 60.
A 12-minute AMRAP, a 10-minute alternating EMOM and a capped For Time. The For Time has no fixed length.
rounds max cut off at 270 s mid-exercise, then a 120 s block padded with 60 s of rest.
A self-paced list run by a clock of 3 x (120 s work, 30 s water), final rest skipped.
Group workout: two zones of two stations, 15 s moves inside a zone, a 30 s water break between zones. 255 + 225.
Two stations, two rotations, transitions [15 s, 30 s water] used in turn. 120 + 135 + 120 + 105.
Two lanes of the same length: a 2-round block and one 60 s row. 60.
Individual mode: a whiteboard lane finishes 30 s early, and nothing is added to its list. A rest follows the node at 90. 90 + 30.
Lanes longer than the primary. Sets of 40 s are cut at 60, so the second is marked cut and the third is gone. Steps of 30 s end exactly at 60, so nothing is marked. 60.
Looping lanes written out in full. A 40 s pass repeats to 100, with its last work cut to 20 s and its rest gone. A lane with its own rounds keeps rounds and repeats apart in iteration. 100.
primary: 1. The first lane's 120 s is cut at the second lane's 90 s. 90.

Lanes in 2 rounds. The rest inside a lane doesn't end the round, so the rest between rounds is added rather than replacing it, skipLastRest leaves it alone, and outer defaults reach into the lane. 30 + 30 + 30.
A rep-based primary lane. The node's length isn't known, so a looping lane shows one pass with loop: true, nothing is cut, and what follows the node has no start.

A timed primary lane, with rep-based steps in other lanes. The total is known. Past the reps a lane's position isn't, so its 100 s step isn't cut, and a rep-based looping lane shows one pass with loop: true. 60.
A 50 s block cuts through a 60 s node 10 s in, which cuts every lane at 40 s. 10 + 40.
Lanes inside a lane. The outer primary's 25 s cuts the inner node at 15 s, and each of its lanes with it. 25.
Lanes at a station count as one 40 s station. The rest inside a lane gets no cue and the transition is added after the node. The other station's 30 s is padded to 40. 40 + 10 + 40.

invalid.description: rounds must be a whole number or "max", not a string number.
A step has exactly one end condition.
rounds "max" on a block needs end.time.
Unknown fields are errors in the schema, so typos such as skipLastrest are caught.
ref must be pwf: plus a kebab-case slug.
The plan is nested at most 16 levels deep, and this one has 17. The schema can't check it, so only a validator rejects it.
One pass of the timeline has at most 100,000 segments, and this one would have a million. A validator must stop expanding it early.
One pass of the timeline lasts at most 24 hours, and this one lasts 25.
The primary lane decides when the node ends, so it can't repeat until then.
A looping lane that plays for zero seconds would repeat forever.
The segment limit counts every lane, even one that would be cut short.
Nine 1 s looping lanes for a day make 777,600 segments. A validator must stop expanding them early.
The 24-hour limit applies to the primary lane, which decides the length.
A task is one list on one clock, so its list can't hold lanes.
A task's clock can't hold lanes.
Stations share one clock, so each needs a fixed length.
A block with rounds: "max" needs timed content to know when to stop.
